response.consequence: Very deep traces (over 1000 levels) can be flushed as several fragmented segments instead of one. This is an unlikely case, but it is a regression from the previous limit.
response.explanation: The loop that follows the redirect chain in add-buffer.lua now stops after 1000 hops, down from 10000. The change did not touch redirect-chain resolution, and nothing in the diff explains the lower bound. If a trace has a parent chain deeper than 1000 spans, the loop exits before it reaches the chain's root set. The span is then written to an intermediate set key. The same logic means those deep subtrees are never merged into one segment.
response.title: Redirect-chain depth limit cut from 10000 to 1000

response.consequence: An admin request with optimized_pagination=true and a negative-offset cursor returns a 500 instead of a page. The "optimized" feature cannot work as documented. The claimed ability to read beyond normal pagination bounds is unsupported.
response.explanation: When enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset < 0, get_result calls queryset[cursor.offset:stop] with a negative start. Django querysets don't support negative indexing, so this raises ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported."). The comment claiming the ORM handles negative slicing is wrong. The cursor offset comes from the client's cursor query parameter. The endpoint passes enable_advanced_features=True whenever optimized_pagination=true and the user is an admin. A cursor such as `0:-5:0` therefore reaches this slice. When stop is also negative or zero the slice is nonsensical as well. The same negative slice is reachable in the else branch for is_prev cursors, and in BasePaginator.get_result, which now passes the raw offset through when cursor.is_prev.

other_findings.consequence: Requests that previously succeeded could return 500 even though they never asked for the optimized path.
other_findings.explanation: `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` runs on every request, including those without optimized_pagination=true. For a non-superuser caller whose organization_context.member is None, such as an API or org-token caller that isn't an org member, this raises AttributeError. Before the change, those callers reached the plain DateTimePaginator path without error. I did not check whether member can be None for this endpoint's permission classes.
other_findings.title: Admin check is evaluated eagerly and can fail the default path when member is None
